runform.title_hint: Empty field: a cheap model derives a short title from the prompt (Settings → Run titles). Every title can be renamed later in the overview.
goal.legend: Goal (optional) — when is this run done?
goal.ph: all tests in test/ pass and the branch is pushed
goal.hint: Typed into the session as "/goal <condition>" right after the start. Claude then checks after every turn whether the condition holds and keeps taking turns by itself until it does — or until it judges it impossible. Only Claude Code knows this; the field disappears for every other coding agent.
goal.title: Goal
goal.pending: not sent yet — waiting for the session
goal.never_sent: never sent: the run was over before the session took it
runform.pipeline_on_hint: Pipeline is on — scheduled starts run as well.
runform.pipeline_off_hint: Pipeline is off — that only gates the scheduled agent starts; this run is not held up by it.
start.mode_idle: as soon as no other run of this repo is going
start.idle_hint: The run waits in the overview and starts by itself as soon as the repo is free. Several waiting runs start one after another, not at once.
start.err_at: Start time is missing or unreadable.
start.err_in: The number of minutes must be greater than 0.
start.until_free: starts as soon as the repo is free
start.err_not_deferred: Only a deferred run can be started this way.
start.err_not_scheduled: Only a planned run can be started this way.
run.terminal_after: (the run is over — the coding agent is still sitting in its session)
run.terminal_mouse_agent: Give the mouse back to the agent in the session
run.terminal_mouse_select: Let the mouse select text here (the agent in the session stops receiving it)
run.session_after_hint: This run is finished and its report is written. Whatever you send here is follow-up work in the same session: when the agent reports done again, it arrives as a follow-up report of this run — checked, merged and announced like the first one, labelled as a follow-up. The session closes by itself once the keep time is up (Settings → tmux session).
run.notify_on_hint: Unticked: no messages about this run — its reports, follow-up reports, alarms and incidents — on any channel. Everything else (integration, flows) happens as usual.
run.end_session_hint: frees the memory of the process still sitting there; log, report and the record of this run stay
run.send_text_ph: Send text into the session (multi-line possible)
run.retry_hint: starts the same task again; an existing worktree is reused
run.archive_hint: An archived run is hidden from the overview but stays fully readable here.
run.agent_waiting: The coding agent finished its turn and has been waiting for input since {ts}. Whatever you type into the terminal reaches it directly.
run.followup_banner: ↻ Follow-up work in progress — this run finished its first task; it reports again the same way (`fl-report done`).
anomaly.followup_overrun: follow-up far over the expected duration
run.resuming: session lost — resuming in a new one
run.harness_not_configured: Coding agent "{harness}" is not configured or disabled — add it under Settings → Coding agents.
run.no_launch_spec: Coding agent "{harness}" cannot be started: bin/fl-start has no case for it and the plugin declares no launch spec (see docs/plugins.md).
sandbox.reason.not_scanned: This machine has not been checked for a container runtime yet.
sandbox.reason.switched_off: The sandbox is switched off for this hub process (FREILAUF_SANDBOX_OFF).
sandbox.reason.no_runtime_module: This hub carries no container-runtime module, so it cannot drive a sandbox.
sandbox.reason.hub_off: The sandbox is switched off for this hub (Settings → Sandbox).
sandbox.reason.harness_unsupported: This coding agent cannot be run in a sandbox: its plugin declares none.
sandbox.launch.module_missing: The sandbox module {module} is not available on this hub.
sandbox.launch.runtime_required: This hub requires every run to be sandboxed, but no container runtime is available ({reason}). Install one, or set the sandbox mode to “available”.
sandbox.launch.runtime_unreachable: The container runtime did not answer, so {container} could not be prepared. Freilauf will try again.
sandbox.launch.proxy_unavailable: The network mode “{mode}” needs an egress proxy, and none could be started.
sandbox.launch.proxy_failed: The run’s egress proxy could not be started: {reason}
sandbox.launch.inject_needs_engine: This profile keeps the credentials out of the container (secrets: inject), which the proxy engine “{engine}” cannot do. Choose an engine that terminates TLS, or a profile that passes the credentials in as environment variables.
sandbox.launch.inject_unsupported: This profile keeps the credentials out of the container (secrets: inject), but the proxy cannot be told what to substitute. The run was not started rather than started with the real key inside it.
sandbox.launch.inject_no_declaration: This profile keeps the credentials out of the container (secrets: inject), but nothing declares how {vars} may be swapped in — the plugin names no header and no hosts for it. The run was not started: a placeholder nobody substitutes makes every call fail as if the provider were down. Use a profile with secrets: env for this coding agent.
sandbox.launch.inject_failed: The credentials could not be handed to the run’s egress proxy: {reason}
sandbox.clone.failed: The sandboxed working copy could not be created: {err}
sandbox.clone.outside_root: Refused to remove {dir}: it is not inside {root}.
sandbox.lifecycle.mem_unknown_why: The container runtime did not answer, so this run's memory is not known. The pane holds only the client process — its size would understate the run about twentyfold.
sandbox.lifecycle.total_incomplete: {n} session(s) could not be measured — the total is incomplete
sandbox.lifecycle.dirt_unknown: The working copy could not be read, so it is not known whether anything is uncommitted — nothing was merged. Check the run’s directory by hand, or start it again.
run.edit.duration_hint: Sets the traffic-light thresholds and the overview's expectation from now on. The running agent is not told.
run.edit.prompt_hint: The run has not started yet — it will launch with this prompt.
run.edit.repo_hint: Moves the run to another repo; the planned start time stays.
run.edit.start_hint: Only a planned run's start time can be changed. "immediately" starts it right away.
run.edit.duration_only_planned: A run that is already over cannot be given a new expected duration.
run.edit.prompt_only_planned: Only a run that has not started yet can be given a new prompt.
run.edit.repo_only_planned: Only a run that has not started yet can be moved to another repo.
run.edit.start_only_scheduled: Only a run that is still waiting for its start can be given a new start time.
run.edit.branch_only_planned: Only a run that has not started yet can be given a new branch rule.
run.edit.duration_invalid: The expected duration must be at least 1 minute.
skills.title: Extra skills
skills.legend: Extra skills (opt-in, become an instruction in the prompt)
flskills.auto: Keep them up to date automatically
flskills.auto_hint: refreshed at every start and after every plugin change; switched off, the copies stay as they are
flskills.conflicts: Freilauf could not write these directories — something is already there that it did not create, and it will not overwrite or remove somebody else's skill. Rename or remove them by hand if you want Freilauf's version there.
flskills.foreign: {n} of these copies were installed by a DIFFERENT Freilauf installation on this machine (data directory: {where}). Freilauf has not touched them: overwriting them would also overwrite the address that installation’s skills read, and the two would keep taking the directory from each other.
flskills.foreign_adopt: They are mine — update the configuration
flskills.foreign_leave: If they really belong to another installation, leave them: this one simply will not manage those directories.
flskills.install: Install the Freilauf skills for my coding agents
flskills.install_hint: switching this off removes exactly the copies Freilauf wrote
flskills.intro: Freilauf ships agent skills: instruction files that teach a coding agent how to drive this hub — find and read runs, create and edit agents and repositories, build flows, read the statistics, and pick a sensible model for a task.
flskills.intro2: This is optional, and it is off until you switch it on. Freilauf then copies the skills into the directories your configured coding agents read — one copy per directory, never one per coding agent. They are user-level, so every session of those coding agents sees them listed — the descriptions all name Freilauf, so nothing else reaches for them.
flskills.user_level: They are installed at user level, so every project you work in has them — there is nothing to add per repository. Choosing them per project is not supported at the moment; if you would like that, please open an issue:
flskills.no_targets: No coding agent is switched on, so there is nowhere to install to. Switch one on under Settings → Plugins.
flskills.shared_note: One more is installed alongside them: a shared reference the skills above load themselves. You do not pick it, so it is not listed here.
flskills.not_configured: Not switched on, and therefore not served: {agents}
flskills.project_hint: These are the directories the same coding agents read inside a checkout. Freilauf never writes into a repository — they are listed so you know where to put a skill of your own.
flskills.remove_body: These directories will be deleted. Only copies Freilauf wrote are touched; a skill of your own with the same name is left alone.
flskills.remove_foreign: (not written by Freilauf — will be left alone)
flskills.skipped: Not served, because the plugin declares no skill directory: {agents}
flskills.pick_hint: Tick the ones you want. Unticking one removes that copy on the next save; the others stay.
flskills.pick_off: Switch the installation on above to choose which of these you want.
flskills.update_paused: Automatic updating is paused for the directories in question above. Freilauf will not touch a copy another installation wrote until you have answered — answer it, and updating resumes by itself.
flskills.synced: Done — the directories now match the settings.
flskills.targets_hint: Which directories a coding agent reads is part of its plugin. Freilauf picks the smallest set of directories that covers every coding agent you switched on, so a skill is never installed twice for the same agent.
flskills.title: Freilauf skills
incidents.title: Incidents
incidents.needs_you_hint: Login, credits or model: this does not clear itself — every following run walks into the same wall. Mark it handled once you have dealt with it.
incidents.noticed_hint: The hub carried on by itself (deferred, retried, or the agent simply kept working). Kept as history and closed automatically once the run finishes.
incidents.resolve_hint: Clearing an entry only silences it here and in the notifications — it changes nothing about the run. If the problem occurs again, the entry reopens and notifies again.
repos.name: Name
repos.extras_invalid: Worktree extras: expected a list of {"path": "…", "mode": "copy"|"link"}.
repos.extras_json: Worktree extras are not valid JSON: {err}
repos.extras_find_hint: a model looks at the repository and suggests what a worktree should carry — the current list is REPLACED
repos.extras_dialog_hint: The hub first checks that the path exists and is a git repository; only then does a model look at the repository and suggest extras.
repos.extras_warn: This completely replaces the current worktree extras. A model generates the whole list from scratch — existing entries are not kept.
repos.extras_working: Looking at the repository and asking the model …
repos.extras_llm_off: Worktree-extras LLM is switched off, or its model provider has no key (Settings → Worktree extras).
repos.extras_parse: The model answered something that is not JSON.
repos.prompt_label: Repo prompt (added to every run of this repo — agents and single runs alike)
repos.merge_flows_none: No flow runs after a merge of this repo.
sessions.title: tmux sessions
sessions.intro: Every run works in its own tmux session, and it deliberately outlives the agent so the screen stays readable. Until it is closed, the agent's process keeps its memory — this is where you end them, oldest first.
sessions.show_running: Also show sessions with a running agent
sessions.auto_hint: Finished sessions close by themselves after {hours} h.
sessions.hidden_note: Sessions with a running agent right now: {n}. They stay hidden by default so none is ended by a misclick.
sessions.unknown_hint: no run of this hub — only ended by hand
sessions.aborted_note: The tmux session was ended before the run reported a result. The run therefore counts as aborted.
settings.global_hint: These settings apply globally to the whole hub — not to the repo selected above. Repo-specific are only the entries under Repos (path, base branch, worktree extras, repo prompt) and the agents themselves.
settings.plugins_hint: coding agents, model providers, their credentials and the installed plugin packages
settings.format_hint: How times, numbers and percentages are displayed. Timezone: Auto follows the UI language (German → Europe/Berlin, Chinese → Asia/Shanghai, English → the server's timezone). An explicit choice always wins.
settings.numbers_hint: Numbers and percentages use the separators of the UI language (a decimal comma in German, for example).
settings.schedule_catchup_hint: After a restart the hub looks this far back for cron and weekly slots that fell into the downtime and starts each affected agent once (its newest missed slot). 0 = never catch up.
settings.gates_hint: A gate defers a start when the account behind that provider is nearly exhausted. Each gate is optional: switch it off and starts pass regardless of the window. Deferred runs can be started anyway from their detail page.
settings.gates_none: No coding agent and no model provider currently declares a budget gate. Switch one on under Plugins and its thresholds appear here.
settings.gate_claude_7d_hint: The general week; a run on a per-model week is measured against its own threshold.
settings.gate_claude_fable_hint: Own threshold for the Fable week. Empty = the 7-day threshold applies.
settings.gate_deepseek_min_hint: A CNY-only DeepSeek account reports no USD — the gate stays open there.
settings.gate_cursor_pct_hint: Percent of the included amount. Cursor reports the included amount from the account; only when it stays silent does "Cursor subscription" step in.
settings.session_keep_hint: 0 = close it right away. Counts from whichever comes first: the run's end or the exit of its process. Sessions are listed and ended by hand under Sessions.
settings.archive_session: Close tmux sessions of archived runs
settings.archive_session_hint: Archiving a finished run closes the tmux session it left standing. Off: an archived session follows the ordinary retention like any other.
settings.archive_session_keep_hint: 0 = close it right away when the run is archived. Counts from the archive.
settings.flow_runs_keep_hint: Finished flow runs (done/stopped) older than this are deleted; failed ones are kept 4× as long so a problem stays visible. 0 = keep forever.
settings.prompt_suffix: Platform prompt suffix — added to the built-in platform rules for every run (placeholders {run_id} {workdir} {report_file} {report_detail_file} {branch_rule} {expected_minutes}). The rules themselves, and the finishing command, always stay; for rules that only concern one repository use the repo prompt.
settings.public_hint: The links in notification messages point at this hub. By default they use the local address; set a hostname here when a name in your DNS (or hosts file) matches the certificate — the port always comes from the live VPN port.
settings.public_host_hint: The run links then look like: {url}
settings.llm_hint: The scanner finds lines that look like a rate limit or provider error. With the check LLM on, it receives the last terminal lines and decides in a structured way whether the agent is really blocked (immediately red) or whether it was a menu line/retry (no incident). Off: hits turn yellow and become red after repetition or 5 min of silence. Applies to all agents. At most one request per run and 10 minutes.
settings.llm_source_explain: Who answers this question for the hub. A model provider is the service that runs the AI model and bills for it — OpenRouter or DeepSeek, for example. A coding agent can answer too, on the subscription you already pay for.
settings.llm_source_overhead: A coding agent starts a whole session for one question — slower and more expensive than a model provider. Good for trying the hub out with a subscription you already pay for.
settings.llm_missing_key: OpenRouter has no API key here — set one under Plugins, or pick another model provider above.
settings.llm_mru_hint: list: the 10 most recently saved models
settings.llm_or_provider: Fixed serving provider ("auto" = best selection per model)
settings.llm_fallback_hint: Tried when the model provider above is unreachable (outage, rate limit, timeout) — before any retry. A coding agent works here too, on the subscription you already pay for.
settings.llm_fallback_model_hint: empty = the model above, or the fallback agent's own default when it needs none
settings.title_hint: A single run whose title field stayed empty gets one from the prompt. A very cheap model is enough for this — a title costs a fraction of a cent. Off, without a key or on any error the run keeps the first line of its prompt as its title; nothing ever fails over a title.
settings.title_model_hint: empty = {model}; the list holds the default and the models saved most recently
settings.extras_hint: The repo form's "Find worktree extras" asks a model to look at the repository and suggest what a worktree should carry beyond what git tracks (a .env, a linked node_modules). Off, without a key or on any error the button simply reports the reason — nothing else depends on it.
settings.extras_model_hint: empty = {model}; the list holds the default and the models saved most recently
settings.llm_ops_legend: When a model does not answer properly
settings.llm_ops_hint: The hub asks for one JSON document and gets prose, a code fence or a truncated answer often enough that it is worth a rule. Applies to all of the hub's own questions above.
settings.llm_retries: Ask again on a broken answer
settings.llm_retries_hint: How often the hub sends the answer back with the exact complaint and asks once more. 0 = never; 1 catches almost everything.
settings.llm_retry_attempts: Attempts when a provider is down
settings.llm_retry_attempts_hint: After the fallback (if any) also failed, the chain is tried again: exponentially increasing pauses with jitter, at most this many attempts per question in total (hard cap 10). 0 = the chain once, no retries.
settings.llm_retry_base_hint: the pause doubles with every round (with jitter), capped below
settings.llm_retry_max_hint: the ceiling the doubling stops at
settings.llm_alert_hint: A provider that has gone wrong goes wrong for every run — without a limit it would send hundreds of identical messages. The hub therefore sends one per kind of failure per window and counts the rest into the next message.
settings.llm_alert_window: One message per failure every … minutes
ca.title: Coding agents
plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.intro: Everything Freilauf can drive lives here: the coding agents that write code on your machine, the model providers that run the AI models, and the plugin packages that add more of either. What is switched on here is what the forms offer you.
plugins.found_explain: Freilauf looked around and found these. Nothing is used until you add it here. You are asked once — "Not now" makes a suggestion stay away.
plugins.found_bin: The command {bin} is installed on this machine.
plugins.found_bin_path: The command {bin} is installed on this machine, at {path}.
plugins.found_env: The environment variable {name} is set. Freilauf reads the name only — never the value.
plugins.never_scanned: This machine has not been scanned yet.
plugins.agents_explain: A coding agent is a command-line programme that writes code on your machine, like Claude Code or opencode. Freilauf starts one per run, in its own tmux session and its own git worktree. Switch on the ones you have installed.
plugins.providers_explain: A model provider is the service that runs the AI model and bills for it — for example OpenRouter or DeepSeek. The coding agent asks it for every answer, so it needs a credential: an API key, either from an environment variable or stored here.
plugins.packages_explain: A plugin package is a directory on this machine holding a plugin.json and its code. Installing one copies it into Freilauf's plugin directory; from then on it appears above like any built-in one. A package that could not be loaded is listed with its error rather than silently ignored.
plugins.attention: Reports when it waits for input
plugins.attention_none: Does not report whether it is working or waiting for input — its runs display as running until they report. See docs/plugins.md, "Attention".
plugins.not_configured: Not configured yet — switch it on and save to use it.
plugins.none_registered: No plugin of this kind is registered.
plugins.providers_hint: Which providers this coding agent may be run with. The run form offers exactly these, and only those whose credential is available.
plugins.providers_agent_own: {agent} keeps credentials of its own, and Freilauf has asked it which model providers those cover. The line under each provider says who supplies the key.
plugins.providers_agent_none: {agent} brings no credentials of its own: Freilauf supplies the key for every model provider it is run with. They are set up under "Model providers" further down.
plugins.no_providers: This coding agent runs on its own subscription — there is no provider to choose.
plugins.credentials_explain: Where Freilauf gets this plugin's API key. Naming an environment variable is the better answer wherever the machine can be given one — the key then never lies in Freilauf's database. Where it cannot, store the value here.
plugins.cred_declared: The plugin reads these variables by itself: {names}
plugins.cred_envvar_hint: Leave empty to fall back to the variables the plugin reads by itself.
plugins.cred_value_hint: Never shown again. Leave it empty and the stored value stays as it is.
plugins.cred_missing_optional: no key — and none is needed
plugins.cred_optional: This key is optional — the model provider works without one too.
plugins.cred_zen_optional: Without a key OpenCode Zen answers with its free models. A key adds the paid ones and the higher limits that come with them.
plugins.badge_llm: Can answer the hub's own questions
plugins.badge_llm_hint: The hub itself asks a small model a few things: a name for each run, whether a log line is a real outage, what a report contains. This provider can do that.
plugins.badge_balance_hint: This provider reports how much credit is left on the account. The sidebar shows it, and the budget gate can defer runs before it runs out.
plugins.forget_hint: Takes it out of Freilauf’s selection and forgets what was configured for it. Nothing is deleted from this machine — the programme stays installed, and you can add it back at any time.
plugins.forget_confirm: Remove {label} from Freilauf’s selection? Nothing is deleted from this machine: the programme stays installed, only what you configured here is forgotten. You can add it back at any time.
plugins.uninstall_hint: This plugin came as a package. Deleting it removes its directory from this machine for good — which is more than taking it out of the selection.
plugins.uninstall_confirm: Delete the plugin package {label} from this machine? Its directory and its configuration are deleted for good. This is not the same as taking it out of the selection.
plugins.pkg_none: No external plugin package is installed.
plugins.errors_explain: What went wrong while loading plugins, in the plugin author's own words. Nothing here stopped the hub — one broken package must never cost you the others.
plugins.install_explain: Point at a directory on this machine that holds a plugin.json. It is checked first and copied only then — a package whose id collides with one that is already there is refused, never silently put in its place.
plugins.install_path_hint: The directory holding plugin.json — not the file itself.
plugins.builtin_note: The plugins that ship with Freilauf are part of it and cannot be removed — switch one off instead.
plugins.problem_no_path: Please give the directory the package lies in.
welcome.title: Welcome to Freilauf
welcome.q1: Welcome — let's get Freilauf set up
welcome.q2: We found these coding agents on your machine. Which of them may Freilauf use?
welcome.q3: Which model provider should Freilauf use?
welcome.q4: Who should answer Freilauf's own questions?
welcome.q5: Should Freilauf teach your coding agents how to drive it?
welcome.q6: That is the setup — one last thing
welcome.hide_hint: You can always come back to this page at /welcome.
welcome.leave_body: You can leave the setup and look around Freilauf first. But until at least one coding agent is switched on, Freilauf cannot start a single run — the pages will all be there, and all be empty. Nothing you have decided so far is lost, this setup greets you again on your next visit, and it is reachable at /welcome at any time.
welcome.revisit_note: You have already been through this setup, so this is an ordinary page: change what you like, or go back. To stop being greeted here, tick "Do not show this again" below and use the button next to it.
welcome.ack_agents: Saved — Freilauf may now use these coding agents: {names}
welcome.ack_agents_none: No coding agent is switched on yet — without at least one, Freilauf cannot start a run. You can pick one under Settings → Plugins at any time.
welcome.ack_provider_none: No model provider is set up. That is fine if you only use Claude Code or cursor — both bring their own subscription.
welcome.ack_llm_all: Saved — Freilauf's own questions are answered by {name}.
welcome.ack_llm_split: Saved — run titles: {title}; incident check: {check}; report contents: {extras}.
welcome.ack_llm_none: Nothing is set up to answer Freilauf's own questions yet. Run titles and the incident check simply stay switched off until something is.
welcome.ack_skills: Saved — the skills are installed in: {dirs}
welcome.ack_skills_empty: Saved — the skills are switched on. They are installed as soon as a coding agent is configured.
welcome.ack_skills_none: The skills stay switched off. Settings → Freilauf skills switches them on whenever you want.
welcome.s1_title: Stop managing agents. Let them run free in your project.
welcome.s1_body: Imagine: you no longer have twenty terminals open at once. You have one place where you hand out recurring jobs — find and eliminate dead code, raise the test coverage, fix bugs — and with every job you define an agent that works on your project regularly, even while you sleep. Freilauf runs those agents on this machine: each run in its own tmux session and its own git worktree, started on schedule or at the push of a button, watched while it works, its report collected, its work merged — and you are notified when something needs you. You set it up once. Then you watch it work.
welcome.s1_why_body: Freilauf is German for a bicycle's freewheel: the part that keeps rolling when you stop pedalling. It is not the absence of control — it is a ratchet: it lets the wheel run free, and only ever forward. A run is done only when its work has arrived, and no agent ever merges or pushes to your base branch — Freilauf does.
welcome.s1_agent_title: The fastest way: let a coding agent set this up
welcome.s1_agent_body: The repository contains a document written for a machine to read, not a human: SETUP_WITH_AGENT.md. Hand it to a coding agent — Claude Code, opencode, cursor — and say "set this up for me". It explains how Freilauf works and what has to be installed and configured, and the agent does the rest. Most people do not know this file exists; it is the shortest path from here to a running Freilauf.
welcome.s2_lead: We had a look at this machine and found the coding agents below. Tick the ones Freilauf should be able to use.
welcome.s2_lead_empty: We had a look at this machine and did not find a coding agent installed. You can still switch one on here and install it afterwards — or install it now and scan again.
welcome.s2_explain: A coding agent is a command-line programme that writes code on your machine, like Claude Code or opencode. Freilauf does not write code itself — it starts one of these and watches it. Tick the ones Freilauf may use; you can change this later under Settings → Plugins.
welcome.s2_none: No coding agent is registered yet.
welcome.s2_all_on: Every coding agent this hub knows is already switched on.
welcome.s2_on_hint: These are already switched on. This setup only ever adds; switching one off again is done under Settings → Plugins.
welcome.s2_never_scanned: This machine has not been scanned yet.
welcome.s2_providers_found: Credentials for these model providers were found too: {names}. The next step sets one of them up.
welcome.s3_explain: A model provider is the service that runs the AI model and bills for it — for example OpenRouter or DeepSeek. The coding agent asks it for every answer, so it needs an API key. Claude Code and cursor bring their own subscription and need none.
welcome.s3_pick: Which one do you want to set up?
welcome.s3_key_found: a key for this was found
welcome.s3_none: No model provider is registered on this hub.

welcome.s4_explain: Besides the agents, Freilauf itself asks a small model a few things: a name for each run, whether a log line is a real outage, and what a report contains. These are short, cheap questions — a fraction of a cent each. Pick who should answer them.
welcome.s4_same: Use the same source for all three
welcome.s4_separate_hint: These are used only when the box above is not ticked.
welcome.s4_check_q: Whether a log line is a real outage
welcome.s5_explain: Freilauf ships a handful of agent skills — short instruction files that any of your coding agents can read. They explain how to list and find runs, how to read a run's errors and check whether its agent is still alive, how to create and edit agents and repositories, how flows and their variables work, and which model to pick for which kind of task. They cost nothing until an agent actually needs them, and everything they say is asked from this hub at the moment it is read, so nothing in them goes stale.
welcome.s5_where: They would be copied into these directories — one copy per directory, chosen so that every coding agent you switched on finds them:
welcome.s5_nowhere: No coding agent is switched on yet, so there is nowhere to put them. Switch one on under Settings → Plugins and Freilauf installs them by itself.
welcome.s5_later: You can change this at any time under Settings → Freilauf skills — switching it off removes exactly the copies Freilauf wrote and nothing else.
welcome.s4_overhead: A coding agent can answer these too, and it works — but it starts a whole session for one question, which is slower and more expensive than a model provider. It is a good way to try Freilauf out with a subscription you already pay for.
welcome.s4_none: Nothing can answer these questions yet. Set up a model provider in the previous step, or switch on a coding agent that can answer them.
welcome.s6_body: Two things are left, and both take a minute: add the repository the agents should work in, then create your first agent — a job, a coding agent, and either a schedule or a button to start it by hand. Notifications are optional: Freilauf runs quietly without one, and Settings → Notifications adds one whenever you want your phone to buzz.

flows.intro: Flows react to finished runs (or a schedule) with no-code building blocks: message running agents, extract structured data from a report, start follow-up agents, send a notification.
flows.name: Name
flows.delete_confirm: Delete this flow? Its past flow runs stay in the history.
flows.trigger.run_merged.desc: Starts once per merge into the base branch, with the run whose work landed — also when a conflict run was needed to make it mergeable.
flows.trigger.manual_hint: Only via "run now" — optionally with a finished run as the simulated trigger.
flows.trigger.unattached: not attached to any agent yet
flows.when.not_done: when it failed or was aborted
flows.attach.hint: When the run has finished, every ticked flow starts — all of them in parallel. The condition here does not replace the "Switch on outcome" block inside a flow; it decides whether the flow starts at all.
flows.attach.none: No flow reacts to finished runs yet.
flows.attach.editor_none: This flow hangs on no agent — it will not start on its own.
flows.attach.editor_hint: Which agents start this flow when their run ends. The very same list is edited in the agent form; a single run picks its flows in the single-run form.
flows.attach.run_none: No flow was attached to this run.
flows.runs.title: Flow runs
flows.editor.name_taken: A flow with this name already exists.
flows.editor.cron_invalid: The cron expression is not valid (5 fields).
flows.editor.variables_hint: Use {{…}} in any text field. Click to copy. Objects render as JSON; missing values as empty text. {{x | default: text}} sets a fallback.
flows.editor.sim_none: run now without a trigger run
flows.editor.run_unsaved: There are unsaved changes — run the saved version anyway?
flows.step.send_message.desc: Types a message into the tmux session of running runs (e.g. "main has moved, please pull").
flows.step.start_agent.desc: Starts a configured agent, optionally with extra prompt text. With "wait" the flow pauses until that run ends and stores its result.
flows.step.start_single_run.desc: Starts an ad-hoc run with its own prompt (as in the single-run form). With "wait" the flow pauses until it ends.
flows.step.kill_run.desc: Kills the tmux session of the selected running runs and marks them aborted.
flows.step.toggle_agent.desc: Switches an agent's schedule on, off or over to the other state, and can start a run right away — but only when no run of that agent is going.
flows.step.extract.desc: An LLM (its model provider is chosen per step, or in the check-LLM settings) reads the report and/or terminal log of a run and fills the fields you define.
flows.step.set_var.desc: Stores a value under vars.<name>. A single {{path}} keeps its type, anything else becomes text.
flows.step.http_request.desc: Calls a webhook/API. The response (status, body, json) is stored in the output variable.
flows.step.shell_command.desc: Runs a command on the hub machine. A non-zero exit code is a result the flow can branch on, not a failure of the step.
flows.step.count_runs.desc: Counts the runs the hub currently has, filtered by repo, status, agent and title prefix — the number a flow needs before it hands out more work.
flows.step.condition.desc: Compares two values and continues in the true or false branch.
flows.step.switch_outcome.desc: Branches on done / failed / aborted (by default the trigger run's outcome).
flows.step.for_each.desc: Repeats the steps inside it once per element of a list — e.g. the open points from an extraction.
flows.step.delay.desc: Pauses the flow for the given minutes (survives a hub restart).
flows.step.notify.desc: Sends a message to the notification channels configured under Settings → Notifications, optionally with an attachment (e.g. the report).
flows.step.note.desc: Writes a line into the flow run log — handy for checking variables.
flows.field.active.hint: "Off" stops the SCHEDULE only — a manual start, a flow start and an API start all still work.
flows.field.startNow.hint: Only after switching on, and only when no run of this agent is running, waiting for help or deferred. Otherwise the step reports it as skipped and the output variable keeps started_run_id empty.
flows.field.wait: wait until the run ends (result → output variable)
flows.field.sourceRun.hint: Run ID or template; default: the trigger run.
flows.field.llmSource.hint: Who runs the model for this extraction. Empty = whatever Settings → check LLM points at. This is not the same as "Source" above, which says where the TEXT comes from.
flows.field.fallback.hint: Tried when the model provider above is unreachable (outage, rate limit, timeout) — before any retry. Empty = the check LLM's fallback from the settings.
flows.field.fallbackModel.hint: empty = the model above, or the fallback agent's own default
flows.field.command.hint: Runs as the hub's user on the hub machine. Templates like {{trigger.merge.sha}} are allowed.
flows.field.cwd.hint: Where the command runs; empty = the hub user's home directory.
flows.field.detach.hint: Start the command in the background and continue at once. Tick this for a command that restarts Freilauf itself and prefix it with "sleep 3;" — otherwise the flow run dies with the hub and stays "running" forever.
flows.field.statuses.hint: scheduled, deferred, running, waiting_help, done, failed, aborted. Empty = every status. An unknown name fails the step instead of widening the filter.
flows.field.titlePrefix.hint: Counts only runs whose title begins with this text; upper and lower case do not matter. Empty = every title.
flows.field.list.hint: Template yielding a list ({{vars.extracted.open_points}}); plain text is split line by line.
flows.field.itemVar.hint: The current element is vars.<name>, its position vars.<name>_index.
flows.editor.var_conditional: set inside a branch or loop — may be missing here
flows.editor.value_none: This operator compares nothing — no value needed.
flows.trigger.cron_no_run: A schedule has no trigger run: {{trigger.run.…}} stays empty, and steps that need a run outcome are only valid after a start step with "wait".
flows.warn.bool_value: {path} is a yes/no value — only "true" or "false" can ever match
flows.warn.number_value: {path} is a number — this value is not one
flows.warn.op_type: This operator cannot answer anything about {path} ({type})
flows.warn.needs_run_maybe: needs a finished run — a manual flow only has one when "run now" is given one
flows.placement.needs_run.rule: Needs a finished run: either from the trigger ("run finished") or from an earlier "Start agent" / "Start single run" with "wait".
flows.placement.needs_run.why: "{step}" cannot sit here: no finished run is available at this point, so the step could only ever take its fallback branch. Put it after a start step with "wait", or give the flow a "run finished" trigger.
flows.placement.needs_run_maybe.why: "{step}" only has a run when "run now" is given one — otherwise it falls through to its fallback.
flows.placement.after_stop.why: Nothing can follow "Stop" — the flow run has already ended there.
flows.placement.needs_run_target.rule: Only the target "the trigger run" needs a finished run. Every other target — an agent, a repo, all running runs, a run ID — reaches runs that have nothing to do with this flow and works in any flow.
flows.placement.needs_run_target.why: "{step}" is aimed at the trigger run, but there is none here. Pick another target — an agent, a repo or all running runs also reach agents outside this flow — or give the flow a "run finished" trigger.
flows.placement.needs_run_target_maybe.w: "{step}" is aimed at the trigger run, which a manual flow only has when "run now" is given one. Any other target works regardless.
flows.warn.needs_run_target_maybe: aimed at the trigger run — a manual flow only has one when "run now" is given one
side.title: Status
settings.abo_price_hint: The monthly price, used to account a run against the subscription.
settings.cursor_included_hint: Included monthly usage — a fallback only: normally Cursor reports it itself.
repos.merge_mode_hint: off: the run ends when the agent reports done; nothing is merged (today's behaviour). hub: Freilauf checks the worktree, merges the run's branch into the base branch itself and escalates only when the agent does not deliver.
repos.merge_check_hint: Shell command run on the merged result before it is pushed, e.g. `node test/unit.mjs`. Empty = none. A red check is treated like a conflict: the agent gets the output and must fix it.
repos.finish_timeout_hint: How long Freilauf waits for the agent to commit or resolve after it reported done. Then it escalates: a conflict run for conflicts, you for uncommitted changes.
repos.merge_max_attempts_hint: How many conflict runs may try before Freilauf asks you.
repos.conflict_parallel_hint: How many conflict runs may work at the same time in this repo. Keep 1 for small repos where tasks touch the same files — parallel resolvers then invalidate each other and only the first one's work survives. Raise it for large repos where conflicts rarely touch the same files.
repos.notify_running: Tell the running agents about a merge
repos.notify_running_hint: After a merge, tell the other running agents of this repo that the base branch moved — urgently if the merge touched files they are working on.
repos.max_parallel_hint: Upper bound of running runs in this repo for scheduled starts; 0 = unlimited. Manual starts are never blocked.
repos.err_number: {field}: a whole number of at least {min} is expected.
merge.settings_intro: When a finished run's branch no longer merges into the base branch and its agent is gone, Freilauf starts a conflict run: an ordinary single run whose whole task is to make that branch mergeable again. This is the setup it starts with — coding agent, provider, model, effort and extra skills.
merge.no_resolver_hint: Without a resolver, a conflicting branch is escalated to you directly.
merge.resolver_prompt: Additional instructions for the conflict resolver
merge.resolver_prompt_hint: Appended to every conflict run's task. Repo rules belong in the repo prompt, not here.
merge.discard_confirm: Discard the uncommitted changes in this worktree? This cannot be undone.
merge.unmerged_both: not merged: commits and uncommitted changes

repos.inactive_no_start: The repository "{name}" is deactivated: no run starts in it. Activate it again on the Repos page.

repos.del_keeps_checkout: Your git checkout is NOT touched, and neither is anything in it:

repos.del_err_confirm: The name did not match. Type "{name}" exactly to delete this repository.
repos.del_err_in_flight: "{name}" still has {n} run(s) going or planned; it cannot be deleted until they are over.

cleanup.target_hint: The agent frees until the total memory is at most this value — oldest inactive first; if those are not enough, younger ones follow.
cleanup.cooldown_hint: After a cleanup run, the next automatic one may start only after this wait — so a run that cannot reach its target does not repeat every 30 s.
cleanup.repo_hint: The agent works in a detached worktree of this repo and never commits — the repo is only the shell.

notify.title: Notifications
notify.intro: Where this hub says things out loud: one card per notification channel it can drive. What is switched on and configured here receives run reports, alarms, incidents and blocked merges.
notify.optional: Notifications are optional. With no channel configured Freilauf does everything it otherwise does — schedule, watch, merge, record — it simply stays quiet. Nothing here has to be filled in.
notify.state_on: At least one channel is configured — messages go out.
notify.state_off: No channel is configured, so the hub stays quiet. That is a complete installation, not a missing step.
notify.add_hint: More channels arrive as plugin packages — install them under
notify.badge_setup_hint: This channel brings a guided setup of its own.
notify.settings_pointer: Notification channels, their credentials and their setup assistants have a page of their own. They are optional: without one the hub simply stays quiet.

notify.telegram_description: Sends messages to a Telegram chat through a bot of your own. It needs a BotFather token and the chat ID; the setup assistant walks you through both.
welcome.s6_faq_hint: Questions? The README has a FAQ — from "can I use my subscription" to "what about security".

sandbox.problem.mount_shape: Every extra mount needs a source and a target: {mount}
sandbox.problem.mount_root: The mount {source} lies outside the allowed directories ({roots}).
sandbox.problem.mount_none: No directory may be mounted into a sandbox on this hub, so {source} is refused. Settings → Sandbox names the allowed roots.
sandbox.problem.mount_traversal: The mount {source} walks out of its directory with “..”.
sandbox.problem.locked: {path} is locked by a policy above and may only be narrowed — it stays {kept}.
sandbox.problem.required: This hub runs every agent in a sandbox, so {layer} may not switch it off.
sandbox.problem.bypass_not_allowed: Switching the sandbox off is not allowed here, so the “off” from {layer} was not applied.
sandbox.problem.harness_unsupported: This coding agent cannot be run in a sandbox — its plugin declares none.
sandbox.problem.hub_off: The sandbox is switched off for this hub.
sandbox.problem.profile_name_missing: A sandbox profile needs a name.
sandbox.problem.profile_builtin: “{name}” is one of the hub’s own profiles and cannot be deleted. Point the repo at another profile instead.
sandbox.problem.profile_delete: The sandbox profile could not be deleted: {error}
sandbox.problem.profile_inject_engine: This profile keeps the credentials out of the container (secrets: inject), and names the proxy engine “{engine}”, which cannot do it — it tunnels HTTPS instead of terminating it, so there is no header to swap. Choose an engine that terminates TLS, or secrets: env.
sandbox.profile.balanced_desc: An allowlist built from the four presets, 8 GB and 4 CPUs. The everyday profile.
sandbox.profile.locked_down_desc: Only the coding agent’s and the model provider’s own hosts — no package registry, 4 GB and 2 CPUs.
sandbox.profile.open_network_desc: No network policy at all; the filesystem and the resource limits are the whole wall.
sandbox.profile.audit_desc: Balanced, but nothing is blocked: every request that would have been denied is written down instead. The mode to roll out in.
sandbox.socket.unauthorized: Missing or wrong report token for this run.
sandbox.socket.no_such_route: This socket carries only the report and sandbox routes of one run; the rest of the API stays on 127.0.0.1.
sandbox.socket.not_sandboxed: This run is not sandboxed: it works on the host, with no network allowlist and no resource limits.
sandbox.socket.ask_hint: If you need a host, a path or more resources, do not work around the sandbox: run fl-report access "<what you need and why>" and carry on with what you can.
sandbox.field.tristate_on: Yes — run this in a container
sandbox.field.tristate_off: No — run this on the host
sandbox.field.tristate_hint: The nearest setting with an opinion decides: this one first, then the agent's, then the repository's — inside whatever the hub's own policy allows.
sandbox.field.hub_required: This hub requires every run to be sandboxed, so it cannot be switched off here.
sandbox.field.hub_default_on: This hub sandboxes runs by default. Switching it off here is recorded as a deliberate exception.
sandbox.field.profile_hint: The profile is the whole rule set — network, filesystem, resources. The overrides below only narrow it.
sandbox.field.profile_none: No profiles configured yet — Settings → Sandbox is where they are created.
sandbox.field.overrides: Narrow the profile for this run
sandbox.field.overrides_hint: A JSON object in the shape of the profile. It may only ever make a locked rule stricter; anything that would loosen one is refused and named.
sandbox.field.unsupported: This coding agent cannot be run in a sandbox — its plugin declares no sandbox support. The run happens on the host.
sandbox.problem.form.required: This hub requires every run to be sandboxed — it cannot be switched off.
sandbox.problem.form.bypass_not_allowed: This hub does not allow opting out of the sandbox.
sandbox.problem.form.harness_unsupported: {harness} cannot be run in a sandbox: its plugin declares no sandbox support.
sandbox.problem.form.refused: This hub's sandbox policy refuses that setting.
sandbox.problem.form.profile_unknown: There is no sandbox profile with the id {id}.
sandbox.problem.flow_overrides: This step's sandbox overrides are not a document this hub accepts, so the run was not started: {problems}
sandbox.problem.form.only_planned: The sandbox can only be changed while the run has not started.
sandbox.problem.form.hub_off: This hub has the sandbox switched off, so a run cannot be put into one.
sandbox.settings.title: Sandbox
sandbox.settings.link_hint: Whether runs happen inside a container, and inside which walls. Currently: {state}
sandbox.settings.intro: The hub layer: what every repository and every run below it may do, and what none of them may loosen. Everything here is optional — with no container runtime on this machine the sandbox stays off and nothing else changes.
sandbox.settings.mode_hint: Cannot be set above “off” while no container runtime is found.
sandbox.settings.mode_available: available — nothing is sandboxed unless asked for
sandbox.settings.mode_default_on: on by default — opting out is a logged act
sandbox.settings.allow_bypass_hint: Off means no repo, agent or run may leave the sandbox, and “Continue without the sandbox” is not offered on a run.
sandbox.settings.runtime_hint: Empty means the one discovery found.
sandbox.settings.lock_hint: One dotted path per line (network.allow, secrets.mode …). A repo, an agent or a run may only narrow these — never loosen them.
sandbox.settings.mount_roots_hint: One path per line. An extra mount is only accepted below one of them.
sandbox.settings.proxy_hint: Every run gets a proxy of its own; the allow list is what it lets through.
sandbox.settings.engine_caps: This engine: TLS termination {tls}, secret injection {inject}, per-method rules {methods}.
sandbox.settings.ca_dir_hint: Where the certificate the proxy presents to the container is kept.
sandbox.settings.ca_dir_unsupported: The engine “{engine}” does not terminate TLS, so it has no use for a CA directory. Its stored value is kept.
sandbox.settings.image_registry_hint: What the images this hub builds are called, e.g. freilauf/agent-base.
sandbox.settings.discovery_legend: What was found on this machine
sandbox.settings.images_hint: Built lazily on first use; a button here builds one ahead of time.
sandbox.settings.err_no_runtime: The sandbox mode cannot be raised above “off” while no container runtime is found. {reason}
sandbox.settings.err_list: {field}: no usable entry could be read out of that.
sandbox.settings.err_build_unavailable: This hub cannot build images: the runtime module does not offer it.
sandbox.page.hub_off: The sandbox is switched off for this hub, so there is nothing to set here.
sandbox.page.unavailable: No container runtime was found, so nothing can run in a sandbox here.
sandbox.page.install_hint: Install Docker (or Podman) and let the hub scan again.
sandbox.page.default_hint: An agent or a single run may still say something else, unless the hub locked it.
sandbox.page.profile_hint: The walls these runs stand in. Edited under Settings → Sandbox.
sandbox.page.builtin_not_deletable: A shipped profile cannot be deleted.
sandbox.page.builtin_copy_hint: This is a shipped profile: saving it writes a copy of your own, so an update of the hub can keep its own defaults current.
sandbox.page.image_hint: An image of your own that carries this project’s toolchain; the agent layer is built on top of it.
sandbox.page.audit_only: Audit only — log what would be blocked, block nothing
sandbox.page.audit_only_hint: The way into an allow list: let a few runs go, then adopt what they really reached.
sandbox.page.merge_check_sandboxed: Run the merge check in the sandbox image too
sandbox.page.merge_check_sandboxed_hint: The check then meets the same toolchain the agent had.
sandbox.page.overrides_hint: A JSON fragment of the profile — only the fields you want different. Empty means: nothing different.
sandbox.page.locked_paths: The hub locked these paths; here they may only be narrowed: {paths}
sandbox.page.err_audit_twice: Audit-only is said twice: by the checkbox and inside the overrides. Say it once — the checkbox is the one that counts.
sandbox.page.dry_run_hint: Starts the image with this policy and no agent, and reports what a run would and would not reach.
sandbox.page.dry_run_intro: What the policy really does, before a run meets it.
sandbox.page.dry_run_none: The dry run reported no checks.
sandbox.page.err_dry_run_unavailable: A dry run needs the sandbox modules, and they are not installed on this hub.
sandbox.page.adopt_title: Hosts these runs reached that are not on the allow list
sandbox.page.adopt_hint: Grown from this repository’s own traffic in audit-only mode. Tick what belongs on the list and adopt it — then switch audit-only off.
sandbox.page.adopt_button_hint: Writes them into this repository’s overrides.
sandbox.page.err_adopt_empty: Nothing was ticked, so nothing was adopted.
sandbox.page.allow_empty: Nothing is on it — this run reaches nothing.
sandbox.page.blocked_title: Blocked while this run was working
sandbox.page.locked_by_hub: The hub locked the allow list, so nothing below it may add to it.
sandbox.page.reconfigure_hint: What can change while the run works does so at once; everything else restarts the container and resumes the agent in its own conversation.
sandbox.page.bypass_hint: Recorded on the run, and reported.
sandbox.page.bypass_confirm: Continue this run without the sandbox? The agent then has this machine’s network and files. It is recorded on the run.
sandbox.page.bypass_forbidden: This hub does not allow leaving the sandbox.
sandbox.page.deny_message: {host} stays blocked — do without it and carry on with what you can.
sandbox.page.err_policy_unavailable: The policy cannot be changed: the sandbox modules are not installed on this hub.
sandbox.page.audit_export_hint: The spec, the proxy log, the container events and the run’s own history as one hash-chained file.
sandbox.page.profiles_hint: A profile is one set of walls under a name. A repository picks one; an agent or a run may narrow it.
sandbox.page.profiles_unavailable: No profiles: the sandbox modules are not installed on this hub.
sandbox.page.profile_spec_hint: Only the fields that differ from the default below. An unknown field is refused rather than ignored.
sandbox.plugin.none: This coding agent declares no sandbox, so its runs always happen on this machine.
sandbox.plugin.state_dirs: What the hub reads back out of the run’s home
sandbox.plugin.cred_claude_oauth_help: Only needed for sandboxed runs. `claude setup-token` prints a long-lived token; stored here, a run in a container authenticates without any credentials file of yours entering it. Leave it empty and claude keeps using its own login, as it always has.
sandbox.plugin.runtime_missing: Sandbox: not available — install Docker (or Podman).
sandbox.page.err_policy_failed: The change could not be applied.
sandbox.reason.ok: A container runtime is installed and answering.
sandbox.reason.no_binary: No container runtime was found on this machine — install Docker (see docs/sandbox.md) and scan again.
sandbox.reason.no_daemon: The container runtime is installed, but its daemon is not running — start it (rootless: systemctl --user start docker) and scan again.
sandbox.reason.unreachable: The container runtime gave no answer at all. Nothing was changed; Freilauf asks again on the next pass.
sandbox.reason.unknown_runtime: Freilauf does not know the container runtime configured here — pick docker, podman or runsc under Settings → Sandbox.
sandbox.reason.unsupported_runtime: The configured runtime is not built yet. Pick docker, podman or runsc under Settings → Sandbox.
sandbox.reason.runtime_not_registered: The daemon answered, but it does not know this OCI runtime — register it (for gVisor: install runsc, add it to the daemon configuration and restart the daemon), then scan again.
sandbox.runtime.build_no_dockerfile: The Dockerfile for “{image}” is not in this checkout ({path})
sandbox.runtime.build_failed: Building {image} failed: {detail} — the whole build log is in {log}
sandbox.runtime.digest_unavailable: The digest of {image} could not be read: {reason}
sandbox.plugin.credential_travels: Inside the sandbox the token never enters the container: the proxy puts it on the {header} header, for {hosts} alone.
anomaly.sandbox_denied: the sandbox got in the way
sandbox.launch.proxy_unreachable: The run's egress proxy would not be reachable from inside the container: the network {network} has no gateway address the hub can listen on ({reason}). Use the iron-proxy engine, or set FREILAUF_SANDBOX_PROXY_BIND to an address the container can reach.
sandbox.launch.proxy_no_egress: The run's egress proxy could not be connected to the network {network}, so it would have no way out itself: {reason}
sandbox.launch.network_failed: The run's private network {network} could not be created: {reason}
sandbox.launch.no_ca: This profile terminates TLS, but no CA certificate is configured. Set the certificate directory under Settings → Sandbox and put ca.crt in it.
sandbox.launch.proxy_gone: This run's egress proxy is no longer running, so the new policy could not be put in force. Restart the run to apply it.
sandbox.launch.builtin_rootless: The built-in egress proxy cannot be reached from inside a container under a rootless daemon: it listens on the host, and a rootless daemon keeps the run's network in a namespace of its own — the hub cannot even bind that network's gateway. Use the iron-proxy engine (it needs an image in FREILAUF_SANDBOX_PROXY_IMAGE), or network mode “open”, or publish the listener yourself at an address the container can reach with FREILAUF_SANDBOX_PROXY_BIND.
sandbox.launch.proxy_reload_refused: The run's egress proxy refused the new network rules, so they are not in force: {reason}
sandbox.launch.limits_failed: The new resource limits could not be applied to this run's container, so they are not in force: {reason}
sandbox.launch.limits_no_container: This run has no container the new resource limits could be applied to, so they are recorded but not in force. Restart the run to apply them.
sandbox.launch.policy_partial: Only part of this change is in force — the rest was recorded and will apply when the run is restarted:
sandbox.launch.spec_write_refused: The run's sandbox.json could not be written — there is a symbolic link at {path}, and Freilauf does not write through one.
sandbox.launch.bypass_resume_failed: The sandbox is off for this run and its container is gone, but the agent could not be relaunched. Retry the run.
sandbox.notify.bypassed: {title}: the sandbox was switched off for this run by {by} — {reason}
sandbox.proxy.config_symlink: there is a symbolic link at {path} where the run's proxy configuration belongs, and Freilauf does not write through one
sandbox.runtime.err_mount_mode: The mount {target} asks for the mode “{mode}”, which is not one this container runtime knows (ro or rw)
